changelog: Explosions land properly, and the bosses have something to say about it. Explosions A blast now detonates across its whole footprint at once — every tile the radius catches, not just the ones that took damage — so shelling empty ground reads as an explosion rather than a single puff. All at once rather than walked outward, because a rocket's splash *is* one blast; staggering the tiles makes a 3×3 look like nine separate shells. The damage numbers now wait for the smoke instead of punching through it. The numbers are the consequence of the shell, so they follow it. It plays at a speed you can read, pinned at one second. The earlier version was sliding rather than stepping, which is why it flickered past. Fog is respected tile by tile. A blast reaches the client if any part of it is visible, so it routinely carries ground you cannot see — drawing there would put an explosion on top of cloud. A blast entirely in fog draws nothing and resolves immediately, so a replay never stalls waiting on one. The bosses talk back Four kinds of line, each with its own trigger. An opening line before the boss takes its first action. The intro prose already existed, but it lives in the pre-battle briefing, which you can skip — so you could fight a commander that never said a word until it happened to play a card. Wound reactions at 75, 50 and 25 percent health. Thresholds rather than per-hit: a boss that grunts at every blow is noise, and the interesting moments are the ones where the fight turns. Losses they notice — the boss remarks when you kill something it commands. Capped at three a battle, because a good turn can clear four units and four consecutive callouts would bury the board. And their card-play pools went from three lines to eight. The old pool looped audibly inside a single fight, so the weakest line was the one you heard most. The writing leans each pool at the mechanic that beats that boss, so the dialogue teaches a little: the Marshal says you keep hitting his thickest side, the Bombardier thanks you for bunching up, the Saboteur tells you to check your hand. A new Warlord frame The old frame carried a winged skull top and bottom, behind all 18 Warlord cards. That is Imperial Aquila iconography — Games Workshop's, not ours — and it should not have shipped. The replacement is a trench parapet: sandbags, barbed wire, duckboards, spent brass, an entrenching tool, a canteen, plain red cloth with no device on it. No eagle, no wreath, no runes, no winged skull. Because card faces composite at runtime now, all 18 cards picked it up without a re-bake. Stepping between cards Opening a card from a grid and then wanting the next one meant close, find, tap again — which is the whole browsing loop of a collection. Chevrons either side, a horizontal swipe, and the left/right arrow keys all step, with an *n / total* under the card. The order is read from the grid you are actually looking at rather than rebuilt, so it can never disagree with it. Under the hood 852 tests. The explosion was verified in a real browser as well as in the suite, since jsdom cannot run a CSS animation.
